faults.finding: 'Every device must break the biggest fault where it sits' ignores Regulation 434.5.1's allowance for a device backed up by one upstream with the breaking capacity.
faults.fix: 'each device … unless a device upstream covers it'; the takeaway says 'normally'; the explain names the back-up allowance.

faults.finding: 'That takes a fraction of a second' is untrue of a distribution circuit allowed 5 s.
faults.fix: 'A fault that clears quickly gives the heat no time to leave.'

faults.finding: 'A breaker past its instant-trip current opens within 0.1 s' is untrue at the bottom of a type C's 5 to 10 In band.
faults.fix: 'past the top of its instant-trip band … For a type C that is 10 × In.'

faults.finding: 'each line's voltage drives through one line's impedance, about half the loop' needs a second reading.
faults.fix: Three short sentences: the neutral carries nothing; the current meets one line's impedance, not a line and a return; that roughly halves the loop and doubles the current.

checked_and_sound: Refresher pattern intact, eleven screens: recall (Cmax against the Cmin and no-factor slips) with Refresh the why / Skip to the practice (screen 6); what it is for with the red consequence; the why with its interactive (Zs slider, the I²t curve against k²S², Cmin and Cmax dots, a still at 0.43 Ω); a judgement check on t (0.1 s against the 0.4 s allowed) and Cmin; the worked heater cpc and the short circuit line by line with the rounded-down figures noted; Section A 2(c), 2(e) and 3(f) with scenario, carried parts and typed answers; Section B on suitable against minimum cpc (five points, any three); one changed-numbers item in the C&G 434.5.2 shape; Keep this.

The causal step is shown: heat is I²Rt, half the area doubles R and halves the copper, so the area is squared; one Zs gives two currents and the larger puts in more heat in the same time, which the dots show crossing the 1.5 mm² line at 0.46 Ω before 0.40 Ω.

The interactive brief names the cause (more fault current as Zs falls) and the effect (Cmax dot over the limit first); the range 0.20 to 1.00 Ω keeps every current past the 16 A type B's 80 A, so 0.1 s holds across it.
